blogs.title: From Tokens to Whole Sentences: Why Sequence‑Level Optimization Matters in RL‑Powered LLMs
blogs.description: A lay‑friendly explanation of the core insight behind GSPO—shifting the importance‑sampling correction from individual tokens to entire generated sequences. The post uses simple analogies (e.g., grading a whole essay vs. each word) and visual diagrams to illustrate why aligning the unit of reward with the unit of optimization stabilizes training.

blogs.title: Taming Mixture‑of‑Experts: How GSPO Eliminates the Need for Routing Replay
blogs.description: An accessible deep‑dive into the specialist/expert routing problem that plagues MoE language models during reinforcement learning. The article walks readers through the expert‑activation volatility issue, explains the previous workaround (Routing Replay), and shows how GSPO’s sequence‑level likelihood ratio naturally sidesteps this complexity.

blogs.title: Why Clipping More Tokens Can Actually Speed Up RL Training
blogs.description: A counter‑intuitive story about clipping fractions. The blog unpacks why GSPO, despite clipping a far larger proportion of tokens than GRPO, achieves higher sample efficiency. It breaks down the mathematics into intuitive graphs and discusses how noisy token‑level gradients waste learning signal.

blogs.title: Simplifying RL Infrastructure: Using Inference Engines Directly with GSPO
blogs.description: Explores the practical engineering benefits of GSPO for large‑scale model training pipelines. Readers will learn how sequence‑level likelihoods tolerate precision mismatches, allowing teams to reuse inference‑engine scores instead of re‑computing token probabilities, thus cutting memory, latency, and engineering overhead.

blogs.title: A Step‑by‑Step Walkthrough of the GSPO Algorithm
blogs.description: A tutorial‑style post that walks developers through the complete GSPO workflow—from sampling a group of responses, computing sequence‑level importance ratios, normalizing advantages, to applying clipping and backpropagation. Includes pseudocode, code snippets in PyTorch, and tips for hyperparameter tuning.
